WHY S27 MUST BE A JUNCTION:
1. SIBLING ISOMORPHISM. circuit_941's two verified siblings are NOT the same
   circuit as each other (circuit_1093 has 10 nets, circuit_560 has 9), so net
   count alone decides nothing here. But testing the component-class-labelled
   netlist graph for isomorphism, over every single flip and every pair of
   flips of the eleven critical sites, gives exactly two hits in the whole
   search space:
       S27=junction alone           -> 10 nets, isomorphic to circuit_1093
       S27=junction AND S31=junction ->  9 nets, isomorphic to circuit_560
   The as-is 11-net reading is isomorphic to neither, and no other site flip
   rescues it. S27 is a junction under BOTH viable readings; only S31 is
   genuinely open, and it is what selects which sibling circuit this is.
2. INK, WITHIN THIS SHEET. S27 does carry a thickening; S31 does not.
   Raw pixels at (696,478): the middle rail is 2 px thick either side of the
   crossing but there are 6 rows of ink (y=479..484) at the crossing, with a
   distinct extra blob at y=483..484, x=693..700 hanging below the rail.
   Raw pixels at (347,494): the column is a uniform 3 px at x=346..348 for
   y=476..490 above the rail AND for y=499..512 below it, with only a 1 px
   transient widening at y=491..495; nothing hangs off the rail at all.
   Normalising the 7x7 core ink by what two plain strokes of the locally
   measured widths would give: S30 (junction) 0.92, S29 (junction) 1.26,
   S26 (junction) 1.18, S27 1.15, S31 0.88. S27 sits with the dotted
   junctions; S31 stands alone at the bottom.
3. THE "SIDEWAYS JOG" AT S27 IS NOT A HOP. inkmap at (696,478) shows the
   column at x=692..694 for y=458..467, widening to x=692..696 for y=468..475
   (a doubled stroke / pen retrace), then x=694..698 through the rail and
   x=696..698 below it: a monotone ~4 px rightward drift spread over 30 px,
   with the doubling 6-14 px ABOVE the rail, not a lateral displacement
   centred on it. A hop is a symmetric arc centred on the crossed wire. There
   is no hop anywhere on this sheet - which is expected, because a ladder needs
   a crossing convention at most at the one floating column.

WHY S31 REALLY IS A CROSSING (independent confirmation of the first pass):
   The verified sibling circuit_1093 is the same generated circuit and the same
   ladder layout, and its GT floats exactly the same node: n9 = {Diode 5 top
   lead, the col-2 upper device} with the middle rail passing under. Cropping
   circuit_1093 at its col-2 / middle-rail intersection (339,488) at 10x shows
   a razor-clean X - two uniform strokes, no blob, no hop - on a sheet where
   that drafter dotted the other four middle-rail column nodes. circuit_941's
   S31 is pixel-for-pixel the same picture on a sheet where this drafter dotted
   the other four. Two independent drawings of one circuit, same ink signature,
   and the verified one is annotated CROSSING. (The other sibling, circuit_560,
   IS a full ladder with col 2 joined - but its drafter dots nothing reliably;
